object.name: evi.hardclip~
object.description: To be used whenever clamping of audio is required, <o>evi.hardclip~</o> should do a good job of protecting your precious audio. This is because this is antialiased hard clipping capable of high input gain whilst maintaining audio quality. <o>evi.hardclip~</o> is the hard clipping section from the <o>evi.clipper~</o> object but with more antiderivative and oversampling options for when managing audio quality against CPU usage, selected via the @aa attribute. Increasing @aa does not necessarily translate to 'better'. Experiment with this setting depending on your audio input material.
object.discussion: This object is for all those MSP users who use [<o>clip~</o> -1. 1.] at the end of their audio chains. You should never do this - it destroys your audio and aliases like hell. Use <o>evi.hardclip~</o> instead. It can anti-alias large gain inputs whilst retaining the clipping functionality you seek.

inlets.digest: Audio Input to be treated nicely

attributes.name: aa
attributes.description: 'aa' stands for 'Anti Aliasing'. Select type (or 'strength') here. 0=1st order antiderivative, 1=1st order 2x oversampled, 2=1st order 4x oversampled, 3=2nd order antiderivative (default), 4=2nd order 2x oversampled, 5=2nd order 4x oversampled.
